findings.detail: Description of "call_tool" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_capabilities, call_tool, run_chain, create_upload_url · Private data: call_tool, run_chain, create_upload_url · Public sink: search_capabilities, call_tool, create_upload_url · Destructive: search_capabilities, propose_capability, suggest_capability, run_capability, get_capability, list_operations, call_tool, run_chain, create_upload_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_capabilities, call_tool, run_chain, create_upload_url · Private data: call_tool, run_chain, create_upload_url · Public sink: search_capabilities, call_tool, create_upload_url · Destructive: search_capabilities, propose_capability, suggest_capability, run_capability, get_capability, list_operations, call_tool, run_chain, create_upload_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "run_capability" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
